clues: Large, spherical, alkaline phosphatase-positive diploid cells first identified in the yolk sac wall during week 3.
They migrate by ameboid movement along the dorsal mesentery of the hindgut to colonize the genital ridges.
They are the embryonic precursors of both oogonia and spermatogonia.
A diploid female germ cell surrounded by a single layer of flattened follicular cells in a primordial follicle.
All of these cells enter meiosis I before birth and arrest in the diplotene stage of prophase I.
It completes meiosis I just prior to ovulation to form a secondary oocyte and the first polar body.
The final metamorphic phase of male gamete formation involving no further cell division.
Haploid round spermatids shed residual cytoplasm, condense their nuclei, and develop a flagellum.
During this process, the Golgi apparatus forms the enzyme-filled acrosomal cap.
A tall columnar somatic supporting cell extending from the basement membrane to the lumen of the seminiferous tubule.
Tight junctions between adjacent cells form the blood-testis barrier.
It responds to FSH by secreting androgen-binding protein and inhibin B, and phagocytoses residual bodies.
A temporary yellow endocrine structure formed from the collapsed wall of a ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation.
Its granulosa lutein and theca lutein cells secrete high levels of progesterone and estrogen.
It is rescued by hCG in pregnancy or degenerates into the corpus albicans if fertilization fails.
A calcium-dependent exocytotic event triggered when a capacitated sperm binds to ZP3.
Multiple point fusions occur between the outer acrosomal membrane and the overlying sperm plasma membrane.
It releases hyaluronidase and acrosin to digest a path through the zona pellucida.
An alteration of the glycoprotein coat surrounding the oocyte immediately following sperm-egg membrane fusion.
It is triggered by exocytosis of lysosomal enzymes from cortical granules into the perivitelline space.
It hardens the matrix and inactivates ZP3 receptors to establish a permanent block to polyspermy.
The eccentrically positioned cluster of pluripotent cells at one pole of the day-5 blastocyst.
It differentiates into a bilaminar embryonic disc composed of epiblast and hypoblast.
Unlike the surrounding trophoblast, this inner cell mass gives rise to the embryo proper.
